title: Same $500, four friends: one made $3,650, one made $511,000
question: Same $500. Four friends.
description: A money parable, not a real business and not advice: four friends start with the same $500 and the same coffee. One owns a cart, one rents five, one gets paid a year in advance, one never touches a cup. Four ideas with a name: organic growth, leasing, pre-selling, and a system.

scenes.narration: Same $500. Four friends. One made $3,650. One made $511,000. Same coffee cart, same year. Here's what each one did.
Friend one bought one cart for $500. About $10 profit a day. 365 times $10, that's $3,650. This is called organic growth.
Friend two rented carts instead, at $100 a year. Five carts, 365 days, $10 each. That's $18,250. This is called leasing.

Friend three rented five too. Then an office tower paid him a year of coffee up front, at 80 cents on the dollar. That rented 146 more. 151 carts, $8 a day. That's $440,920. This is called pre-selling.
Friend four never bought a cart. She sold her recipe and her name. 70 carts pay her $1 a cup, 20 cups a day. That's $511,000. This is called a system.
Same $500. $3,650 against $511,000. The money was the same. The idea wasn't.
It's a parable, not a plan. Which friend are you? One, two, three, or four? Tell me below.
Same $500, four different years. Follow for tomorrow's why.
